maria-infra: Quick update — completed perf validation for the new mia-1 cluster (3 racks, 24 x A100-80G equivalent). Handing off for oncall/ops runbook update and canary planning. Results and notes below.

maria-infra: Summary metrics (inference baseline, p50/p95 measured on internal gpt-compat workload):
- p50 per-request latency (128 tokens): 18ms
- p95 per-request latency (128 tokens): 46ms
- steady-state throughput (tokens/sec, aggregate): 52,000 tps (2.17k tps/GPU)
- GPU util avg: 67% (peak 92% during batching bursts)
- observed OOMs: 0 during 3h soak

sophia-ml: Quality/regression checks: prompt set A (200 cases) — 0 failures vs baseline; small divergence on truncation edgecases, tracked in the eval dashboard.

maria-infra: Kernel/driver/stack checks run:
```
# node sample checks
ssh node-01
uname -a
Linux node-01 6.5.10-rt #1 SMP PREEMPT_RT x86_64 GNU/Linux
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module  535.86.10  Thu Feb  2 2026
CUDA: 12.2, cuDNN: 9.5
```

maria-infra: DCGM health snapshot (trimmed):
```
GPU  Util  Temp  ECC  Power
0    88%   74C   OK   300W
1    65%   72C   OK   295W
...
All NVLink links healthy, PCIe retransmits within normal noise.
```

maria-infra: Perf harness commands used (for reproducibility):
```
# run the inference benchmark harness
./bench/run_infer.py --model gpt-compat-v2 --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --seq-lens 64,128,512 --duration 10800 --workers-per-gpu 2
# collect traces
./tools/collect_traces.sh node-0..node-23 /tmp/mia1-perf-2026-03-05
```

ajay-ops: Network/infra checks — ran iperf mesh between racks: mean 98.7 Gbps, jitter < 150us. No packet loss.

kai-platform: Driver/kernel anomalies? saw 1 kernel WARN on node-17 earlier:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (Cluster) 13, PID 0: Fault on GPU 17: 0x86c0
```
maria-infra: That Xid was during stress-induced MIG reconfigure, traced to transient firmware timing; firmware updated and no repro after. Logged under infra ticket INF-4721.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: redwood/runtime:v2026.3.4 -> mia-1 overlay applied (canaries 3/3 passed). :white_check_mark:

eng-oncall: @eng-oncall taking handoff. Can you paste the short checklist to add to eng-oncall rotation notes?

maria-infra: Added checklist to the runbook (link): https://internal.redwood/runbooks/mia1-provisioning (items below also appended).
- verify driver/CUDA versions (NVRM >= 535.86.10, CUDA >=12.2)
- confirm DCGM health snapshot no GPU ECC errors
- run quick smoke: ./tools/smoke_infer.sh --model tiny --seq 64 --duration 300
- run network quicktest: iperf3 -c rack-peer -t 30
- run node soak: nodetool soak --duration 1h on 2 sample nodes
- tag nodes with capacity class: "mia1-standard-80g"

ajay-ops: Cost note: projected committed monthly cost for this cluster size ~ $210k/mo (pre-discounts). See cost model in the provisioning doc.

sophia-ml: One ML note: recommend enabling tensor-cores batch fusion for production, adds ~12% throughput on seq-128 workloads; we'll prepare a config patch for runtime to toggle.

kai-platform: Created infra task INF-4772 to track automated health checks + grafana dashboard: includes p95 latency, tokens/sec per-rack, GPU temp, Xid rate.

maria-infra: Handoff acceptance criteria met: perf baseline within 7% of expected, no persistent hardware errors, network OK. Marking ready for canary traffic tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

eng-oncall: SGTM. I'll take the first shift for the canary window and escalate to eng-sre if any regressions. Please drop the links to dashboards in the runbook.

ajay-ops: Pushed the small infra tweaks to terraform branch mia1/patch-2026-03-05, ready for review.

maria-infra: Thanks all — tagging final followups: @sophia-ml to send runtime config PR, @kai-platform to attach dashboards, @ajay-ops to confirm cost commit in billing.

eng-oncall: ack, will confirm after first 2h of canary.

maria-infra: Closing this thread; keeping logs at /artifacts/mia1/perf-2026-03-05.tar.gz and runbook updated. Ping me if you need raw traces. :shipit:
